as_written_in_papers.quote: p.Lys260Gln (c.778 A > C in exon 4 of the GFAP gene; K260Q)

cases.statement: Proband (25-year-old woman, adult-onset picture) and her mother, who carries the variant and reports mild symptoms. Only the proband is in the batch.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: incontinence, clumsiness and temperature dysregulation since middle school; dysphagia and dysarthria; seizure-like episode; spasticity and hyperreflexia; MRI periventricular/ependymal T2 signal with medullary atrophy and upper cervical cord wasting

quotes.quote: The patient is a 25-year-old Caucasian female who presented to the emergency department after a witnessed event described as a period of rapid eye blinking and unresponsiveness.

She was followed up in our resident continuity clinic as an outpatient, where a genetic test for AxD was ordered revealing a missense variation in the glial fibrillation acidic protein (GFAP) gene of p.Lys260Gln (c.778 A > C in exon 4 of the GFAP gene; K260Q).
She described incontinence, clumsiness, and difficulty “regulating her body temperature” since middle school.
Despite treatment for these diseases, she continued to have episodic hypothermia, weakness, dysphagia, dysarthria, and spasticity.
Other abnormalities included marked wasting and narrowing of upper cervical spinal cord and medullary atrophy as well as increased signal in the pons and cerebellar peduncles.

people.label: mother of patient
people.key_phenotypes: self-reported decreased balance and coordination and difficulty regulating temperature; no objective data, no MRI

quotes.quote: Her parents were also tested revealing the same mutation in her mother.
On further discussion with the mother, she reported decreased balance and coordination that were out of proportion to her age and “difficulty regulating her temperature.”
No objective data exist for these complaints, and she has not yet had an MRI performed.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Authors state the patient meets the MRI criteria and most clinical findings of adult-onset AxD. An elevated blood silver level (colloidal silver use) was considered and judged not to explain the ongoing symptoms. Which genes were sequenced is not stated ('requested genes').

quotes.quote: The patient described meets the diagnostic MRI criteria and fits the majority of the clinical findings presented earlier, and a genetic sequencing test was done to further solidify the diagnosis.
Her blood silver level was elevated to 9.6 mcg/dL (normal is < 5 mcg/dL).

While some abnormalities in her MRI could be attributable to heavy metal deposition, silver toxicity would not explain her ongoing symptoms; other than pancytopenia, her clinical picture as well as the medullary and cervical spinal atrophy on the MRI were more consistent with AxD.
Using genomic DNA, the coding regions and splice junctions of the requested genes were PCR-amplified, and capillary sequencing was performed.

segregation.statement: Both parents tested; the mother carries the variant and reports unverified mild symptoms (no examination data, no MRI). The father's result is not stated explicitly. A younger sister is said by the parents to be beginning to show dysautonomia; her testing is not reported.

quotes.quote: Her parents were also tested revealing the same mutation in her mother.
On further discussion with the mother, she reported decreased balance and coordination that were out of proportion to her age and “difficulty regulating her temperature.”
No objective data exist for these complaints, and she has not yet had an MRI performed.
There are no other family members with these complaints, although the parents say the patient's younger sister is beginning to show symptoms of dysautonomia.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo: inherited from the mother.

quotes.quote: Her parents were also tested revealing the same mutation in her mother.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, p.(Lys260Gln), exon 4. Authors state the disease is caused by dominant GFAP variants acting by gain of function, and cite nearby missense changes reported in AxD.

quotes.quote: This leukodystrophy is caused by dominant mutations in the GFAP gene and is thought to confer cytotoxicity through gain of function mechanisms [9].
though nearby missense variations (Y257C, R258C/P, and L264P) have been reported to cause AxD [7]

computational_predictions.statement: PROVEAN score -3.49; unnamed conservation and protein predictors reported as supporting a deleterious effect.

quotes.quote: This was determined using the PROVEAN model with a strong supporting score of −3.49.
in silico analyses including evolutionary conservation and protein predictors supported a deleterious effect

population_data_in_papers.statement: Authors state the variant is not reported in gnomAD.

quotes.quote: This particular mutation has not been reported in the Genome Aggregation Database (GNOMAD) or in Clinvar

authors_classification.statement: Testing report classification quoted by the authors, their own conclusion, and a later sentence that qualifies it.

quotes.quote: This was classified as a “likely pathologic variant”
In our patient, the pathognomonic imaging findings, her clinical support, and the presence of a mutation with deleterious effects in simulation strongly indicates that it is a pathogenic variant.

The availability of GFAP gene sequencing has increased the frequency of the diagnosis of this rare disorder, but while a number of other mutational abnormalities have been described, the one described earlier has not been proven to cause AxD [8].

concerns: The paper contradicts itself on family history: it says family history was not significant, then reports a carrier mother with symptoms and a symptomatic younger sister.
The authors both conclude the variant is causal and say it 'has not been proven to cause AxD'.
Carrier mother is not in the batch; she has only self-reported symptoms and no MRI. The sister's genotype is not reported.
Confounders: colloidal silver use with raised blood silver; head trauma with basilar skull fracture and prior traumatic brain injury care.
Zygosity, transcript and testing laboratory are not stated.
notes_for_panel: Inherited from a mildly symptomatic mother; variable expressivity is discussed by the authors. Family-history statement in the case section conflicts with the later family findings.
